cc.attr: Streets, rail, Tevere and Aniene: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). Coast: OSM via @geo-maps. Outer rivers and roads: Natural Earth.
cc.baseOn: Base map: OpenStreetMap — every street in the centre, main roads, rail and the rivers across the city; outside that, Natural Earth (generalised).
cc.extrasNote: Off the planned walks: add them with Custom, or go on their own.
cc.helpNote: Base map: drawn from OSM coastline and Natural Earth (main rivers, roads and rail, generalised; can sit up to about 1 km off). No street map yet. The church hunt is the heart of this map: see Routes › Tours by topic › Church day. Most Catholic churches close about 12:00–16:00; San Gaspare, the Jubilee Church and Hua Yi Si stay open at midday. Pins come from Google Places where possible; approximate ones are marked.

sights.name: Santa Maria Antiqua
sights.blurb: A 6th-century church inside an imperial building at the foot of the Palatine, its walls layered with paintings from four centuries.
sights.when: Forum ticket with the SUPER/Full Experience add-on; booking required; 9:30–18:00. Closed on free first Sundays.
sights.q: Santa Maria Antiqua, Foro Romano

sights.name: San Nicola in Carcere
sights.blurb: A medieval church built straight into three Republican temples; underneath, you walk the alleys between their podiums.
sights.when: Daily except Wednesday 10:00–17:00 (checked May 2026); the underground costs about €3.
sights.q: Basilica di San Nicola in Carcere, Roma

sights.name: San Clemente
sights.blurb: The textbook stack: a 12th-century church on a 4th-century church on a Roman house with a temple of Mithras.
sights.when: Mon–Sat 9:00–12:30 and 14:00–18:00, Sun 12:00–18:00 (Google, 2026); underground about €10 online, €12 at the desk, timed entry.
sights.q: Basilica di San Clemente, Roma

sights.name: Santo Stefano Rotondo
sights.blurb: Rome's oldest round church, 5th century, its walls lined with 34 lettered scenes of martyrs being tortured.
sights.when: Closed Monday; roughly 10:00–13:00 and afternoons (sources disagree: 15:30–18:30 or 14:30–17:30).
sights.q: Basilica di Santo Stefano Rotondo, Roma

sights.name: Case Romane del Celio
sights.blurb: Under the church of Santi Giovanni e Paolo: Roman apartments with a painted Christian shrine on a stair landing.
sights.when: Daily 10:00–16:00 (Google, 2026); ticket with audio guide. Entrance on the Clivo di Scauro.
sights.q: Case Romane del Celio, Clivo di Scauro

sights.name: Catacombs of Saints Marcellinus and Peter + Mausoleum of Helena
sights.blurb: A little-visited catacomb with restored frescoes, joined to the mausoleum of Constantine's mother.
sights.when: Catacomb by booking only (santimarcellinoepietro@gmail.com, +39 339 6528887); closed Thursday and 1–15 Aug, 1–15 Sep; mausoleum alone €3, joint ticket €8–10.
sights.q: Mausoleo di Sant'Elena, Via Casilina 641

sights.name: San Bartolomeo all'Isola
sights.blurb: On the Tiber island, where the healing temple of Asclepius stood: a well-head over the sacred spring and a French cannonball in the wall.
sights.when: Church hours (unchecked).
sights.q: Basilica di San Bartolomeo all'Isola, Roma

sights.name: Santa Passera
sights.blurb: A three-storey stack by the Tiber: medieval church on early-medieval crypt on a Roman tomb. There is no saint called Passera.
sights.when: Sunday Mass 10:30 (not July–September); the lower levels only on guided visits (next announced 28 Nov 2026).
sights.q: Chiesa di Santa Passera, Vicolo di Santa Passera

sights.name: Santa Maria in Aracoeli: the drilled column
sights.blurb: Up 124 steps on the Capitol: a hall of reused Roman columns, one of them bored through. Was it a sundial? Probably not.
sights.q: Basilica di Santa Maria in Aracoeli

sights.name: Sant'Ivo alla Sapienza
sights.blurb: Borromini's university church: a star-shaped plan and a lantern that twists into a corkscrew. Reopened October 2026.
sights.when: Mon–Fri 9:30–13:30, free (reopened 27 Oct 2026, run by Touring Club volunteers). The courtyard can be seen whenever the gate is open.
sights.q: Sant'Ivo alla Sapienza, Corso del Rinascimento 40

sights.name: Sant'Ignazio di Loyola
sights.blurb: The Jesuits ran out of money for a dome, so Andrea Pozzo painted one, flat, on canvas. Stand on the floor disc and it appears.
sights.when: Daily, from 9:00 (Google, 2026); a mirror on a trolley helps you study the ceiling; queues at peak times.
sights.q: Chiesa di Sant'Ignazio di Loyola, Roma

sights.name: Santa Maria dell'Orazione e Morte
sights.blurb: The church of the brotherhood that buried Rome's unclaimed dead; below, a crypt of bones with skulls labelled by date and cause of death.
sights.when: Unclear in 2026: restoration of the interior is under way and one source says it cannot be visited. Crypt hours, when open, are mostly late afternoons. Check before going.
sights.q: Chiesa di Santa Maria dell'Orazione e Morte, Via Giulia 262

sights.name: Santo Spirito in Sassia
sights.blurb: Europe's oldest hospital complex: a 120 m frescoed ward, a church, a medical museum and the stone baby hatch on the street.
sights.when: The complex is by booking only (corsiesistine@aslroma1.it); the outside and the baby hatch any time. The medical museum next door keeps its own hours.
sights.q: Complesso Monumentale Santo Spirito in Sassia, Borgo Santo Spirito

sights.name: Santi Cosma e Damiano
sights.blurb: A Roman library hall turned into a church in 527, with one of the oldest apse mosaics in Rome and a window into a round temple.
sights.q: Basilica Santi Cosma e Damiano, Via dei Fori Imperiali

sights.name: San Crisogono (lower church)
sights.blurb: Under a busy tram stop in Trastevere, a whole 4th-century basilica, entered from the sacristy.
sights.when: About €3; roughly 7–11:30 and 16–19 (sources conflict); restoration was still under way in March 2026.
sights.q: Basilica di San Crisogono, Trastevere

sights.name: Santa Cecilia in Trastevere (excavations)
sights.blurb: Under the church, Roman houses with round basins, plus Maderno's statue of the martyr with the cut in her neck.
sights.when: Daily 10:00–12:30 and 16:30–18:30 (Google, 2026); excavations about €2.50; not during Mass.
sights.q: Santa Cecilia in Trastevere

sights.name: Carcer Tullianum (Mamertine Prison)
sights.blurb: The state prison of ancient Rome, under a 1597 church: a hole in the floor led to the death cell.
sights.when: Daily 8:30–17:00 (Google, 2026); about €10 with a tablet guide. Very small; six people at a time in the lowest cell.
sights.q: Carcere Mamertino, Clivo Argentario 1

sights.name: Catacombs of Domitilla
sights.blurb: About 17 km of galleries on four levels, entered through a 4th-century basilica half sunk into the ground.
sights.when: Daily except Tuesday 9:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00 (Google, 2026); guided only.
sights.q: Catacombe di Domitilla, Via delle Sette Chiese 282

sights.name: San Sebastiano and the Memoria Apostolorum
sights.blurb: Under the basilica on the Appian Way, a 3rd-century hall where pilgrims scratched prayers to Peter and Paul on the walls.
sights.when: Church daily 8:30–18:00; catacomb on its own guided tours (check days).
sights.q: Basilica di San Sebastiano fuori le mura, Via Appia Antica 136

sights.name: Santa Costanza
sights.blurb: The round mausoleum of Constantine's daughter, with 4th-century mosaics of grape harvests still in the vault.
sights.when: Daily 9:00–18:00 (Google, 2026); free; bring coins for the lights.
sights.q: Mausoleo di Santa Costanza, Via Nomentana 349

sights.name: Santi Quattro Coronati
sights.blurb: A fortified monastery on the Celio, built to protect popes; inside, a 1246 chapel painted with the story of Constantine.
sights.when: Church daily from 6:30, closed midday; cloister mornings; the San Silvestro chapel by asking at the nuns' wheel.
sights.q: Basilica Santi Quattro Coronati, Roma

sights.name: Santa Prassede
sights.blurb: A 9th-century church hiding the San Zeno chapel, lined with gold mosaic and including a portrait of the pope's living mother.
sights.when: Church hours (unchecked); coin-operated lights.
sights.q: Basilica di Santa Prassede, Roma

sights.name: San Bernardo alle Terme
sights.blurb: A round church made in 1598 out of a corner tower of the Baths of Diocletian, under a coffered dome like a small Pantheon.
sights.when: Mornings and late afternoons (Google, 2026), closed midday.
sights.q: Chiesa di San Bernardo alle Terme

sights.name: Santi Vincenzo e Anastasio a Trevi
sights.blurb: Facing the Trevi Fountain, the parish church of the papal palace, where the hearts and organs of 22 popes are kept.
sights.q: Chiesa Santi Vincenzo e Anastasio a Trevi

sights.name: Capuchin Crypt
sights.blurb: Six chapels decorated with the bones of about 3,700 friars; the famous one, for comparison with Via Giulia.
sights.when: Daily 9:30–12:30 and 14:30–17:30 (Google, 2026); about €10 with audio guide; cover shoulders and knees.
sights.q: Museo e Cripta dei Cappuccini, Via Vittorio Veneto 27

sights.name: Tempietto di Bramante
sights.blurb: A small round temple in a cloister, built where Peter was said to be crucified; the model for St Peter's dome.
sights.when: Tue–Sun 10:00–18:00 (Google, 2026); free; entrance through the Spanish Academy.
sights.q: Tempietto del Bramante, San Pietro in Montorio

sights.name: St Paul's Within the Walls
sights.blurb: The first non-Catholic church inside the walls after 1870, with Burne-Jones mosaics that give the saints the faces of Lincoln and Garibaldi.
sights.when: Mon–Fri 10:00–15:00, Sunday services (Google, 2026).
sights.q: St Paul's Within the Walls, Via Nazionale 16a

sights.name: San Gioacchino in Prati
sights.blurb: An 1890s church with an aluminium dome pierced by crystal stars, built in the years of the Eiffel Tower.
sights.when: 6:30–12:30 and 16:30–19:30 (Google, 2026). Occasional guided visits to the dome terrace (tripplus.it).
sights.q: Chiesa di San Gioacchino in Prati, Via Pompeo Magno 25

sights.name: Tempio Valdese, Piazza Cavour
sights.blurb: Rome's first church on a reinforced-concrete frame (1911–14), built by Protestants in a style meant to say "church, but not Catholic".
sights.when: Inside Tuesday 17:00–19:00 and Saturday 11:00–13:00 (Google, 2026), or ask at the office Wed–Fri 10:00–12:00 (06 3204868); concerts. The exterior any time.
sights.q: Tempio Valdese di Piazza Cavour

sights.name: Great Synagogue (Tempio Maggiore)
sights.blurb: The 1904 synagogue built where the ghetto walls stood, with the only square dome in Rome, clad in aluminium.
sights.when: Through the Jewish Museum, guided, with a security check: Sun–Thu 10:00–16:00, Fri 9:00–13:00 (Google; winter hours shorter). Closed Saturday and Jewish holidays.
sights.q: Great Synagogue of Rome, Lungotevere de' Cenci

sights.name: Sacro Cuore Immacolato di Maria, Piazza Euclide
sights.blurb: Brasini meant this church to carry a 100 m dome visible across Rome. Only the drum was built; a model of the dream stands inside.
sights.q: Basilica del Sacro Cuore Immacolato di Maria, Piazza Euclide

sights.name: Sacro Cuore di Cristo Re
sights.blurb: Piacentini's brick church of 1920–34, facing the RAI headquarters: a church halfway between tradition and the modern.
sights.q: Basilica del Sacro Cuore di Cristo Re, Viale Mazzini 32

sights.name: Santi Pietro e Paolo, EUR
sights.blurb: The domed travertine church that closes the axis of EUR, the Fascist world's-fair city.
sights.q: Basilica Santi Pietro e Paolo, EUR

sights.name: Santa Rita in Campitelli (Sala Santa Rita)
sights.blurb: A Baroque church that was taken apart and rebuilt 300 m away in 1928, when the Capitol was "cleared"; now an exhibition hall.
sights.when: Only during exhibitions, Tue–Sat 17:00–19:00.
sights.q: Sala Santa Rita, Via Montanara

sights.name: Santi Sette Fondatori
sights.blurb: A round postwar church on Piazza Salerno, white marble below and a lighter drum above.
sights.when: Parish hours.
sights.q: Chiesa dei Santi Sette Fondatori, Piazza Salerno

sights.name: Mausoleo Ossario Garibaldino
sights.blurb: A Fascist-era crypt of 1941 for the dead of the Roman Republic and Italian unification, under a gold mosaic vault.
sights.when: Thursday 9:30–13:30 only (from 23 Sep 2026); closes in bad weather.
sights.q: Mausoleo Ossario Garibaldino, Via Garibaldi 29

sights.name: Santa Maria della Visitazione
sights.blurb: Busiri Vici's raw-concrete church in Casal Bruciato: diagonal piers and wall-beams like the ribs of a ship. The most purely brutalist church in Rome.
sights.when: Winter 7:30–12:00 and 16:30–19:00; June–August 17:00–19:00 only (Turismo Roma).
sights.q: Chiesa di Santa Maria della Visitazione, Via dei Crispolti 142

sights.name: San Vincenzo Pallotti
sights.blurb: A centrally planned church of 1989–93 under a concrete hyperbolic-paraboloid vault, 900 m from the Visitazione.
sights.when: Parish hours.
sights.q: Chiesa di San Vincenzo Pallotti, Via Matteo Tondi 80

sights.name: Nostra Signora de La Salette
sights.blurb: A 1960s church on a lobed oval plan under a tent roof of fair-faced concrete that breaks the light into cones.
sights.q: Chiesa Nostra Signora de La Salette, Piazza Madonna della Salette 1

sights.name: Gesù Divin Lavoratore
sights.blurb: Fagnoni's oval church of 1955–60 for "Jesus the Worker": a stone drum on concrete piers, entered through its bell tower.
sights.when: Parish hours.
sights.q: Chiesa di Gesù Divino Lavoratore, Via Oderisi da Gubbio 16

sights.name: San Gaspare del Bufalo
sights.blurb: One of Pier Luigi Nervi's last works: a square church entered at a corner, under a copper pyramid of prefabricated beams.
sights.when: Open 7:30–21:00 daily (Google, 2026), so a good midday stop. Metro A Arco di Travertino.
sights.q: Chiesa di San Gaspare del Bufalo, Via Borgo Velino 1

sights.name: San Giuseppe Cafasso
sights.blurb: A 1966–70 church by Paniconi and Pediconi under a massive roof that seems to float on four piers.
sights.when: Closed Monday; mostly afternoons 16:30–19:00, plus some mornings (Google, 2026).
sights.q: Chiesa di San Giuseppe Cafasso, Via Camillo Manfroni 2

sights.name: Santa Maria Madre del Redentore, Tor Bella Monaca
sights.blurb: A triangular concrete tent by Spadolini with a roof engineered by Morandi, and no cross on top: two pinnacles cut the sunlight into one.
sights.when: Parish hours; Metro C Torre Angela, then walk or bus.
sights.q: Chiesa Santa Maria Madre del Redentore, Viale Duilio Cambellotti 18

sights.name: Great Mosque of Rome
sights.blurb: Portoghesi's mosque of 1984–95, where the prayer hall is a forest of three-stemmed columns branching like palm trees.
sights.when: Visits Wednesday and Saturday mornings from 9:00 (end time 11:30 or 12:30, sources differ); not during Ramadan or holidays. Shoes off, women cover their heads, modest dress. Roma–Viterbo train to the Campi Sportivi stop.
sights.q: Grande Moschea di Roma, Viale della Moschea 85

sights.name: Dio Padre Misericordioso (Jubilee Church)
sights.blurb: Richard Meier's three white concrete sails, up to 26 m high, set among the blocks of Tor Tre Teste for the Jubilee of 2000.
sights.when: 7:30–19:00 daily (Google, 2026), so a good midday stop; no visits during Mass; free. Metro C Torre Maura, then bus 556.
sights.q: Chiesa Dio Padre Misericordioso, Largo Terzo Millennio 8

sights.name: Santo Volto di Gesù
sights.blurb: A 2003–06 church by Piero Sartogo and Nathalie Grenon, filled with contemporary art, directly across the road from medieval Santa Passera.
sights.q: Chiesa Parrocchiale del Santo Volto di Gesù, Via della Magliana 162

sights.name: San Pio da Pietrelcina, Malafede
sights.blurb: Three tilted parabolic arches of steel that touch the ground only at their ends, roofed with shards of aquamarine tile.
sights.when: 7:00–21:00 (Google, 2026). Far south-west, near the Roma–Lido line; a car or taxi helps.
sights.q: Chiesa di San Pio da Pietrelcina, Via Paolo Stoppa 12

sights.name: Hua Yi Si Buddhist temple
sights.blurb: A Chinese Buddhist temple with pagoda roofs, hidden behind warehouse walls in an industrial zone: said to be the largest in Europe.
sights.when: Daily 10:30–15:00 (Google, 2026), a good midday stop. Shoes off, quiet; men to the right, women to the left during practice.
sights.q: Centro Buddhista Hua Yi Si, Via dell'Omo 142

sights.name: Sacro Cuore di Gesù Agonizzante, Vitinia
sights.blurb: Ildo Avetta's 1955 church in a village-suburb on the Ostia railway, called one of the best Roman churches of its period.
sights.when: 7:30–19:30 (Google, 2026). Roma–Lido train to Vitinia.
sights.q: Sacro Cuore di Gesù agonizzante a Vitinia

sights.name: San Frumenzio
sights.blurb: A 1981–85 church on an elliptical plan under a tent roof with glazed gaps; it keeps the fibreglass models of Nervi's Way of the Cross.
sights.q: Chiesa di San Frumenzio ai Prati Fiscali, Via Cavriglia 8

sights.name: Santa Maria della Presentazione
sights.blurb: A concrete cylinder entered below street level, with a cross of two blades hanging like a stalactite from the dome.
sights.when: Parish hours.
sights.q: Chiesa di Santa Maria della Presentazione, Via di Torrevecchia 1104

sights.name: San Carlo Borromeo, Fonte Laurentina
sights.blurb: Monestiroli's tuff-clad box of 2008–10, where the tower over the altar is both bell tower and skylight.
sights.when: Parish hours.
sights.q: Chiesa San Carlo Borromeo, Via Edoardo Amaldi 215

sights.name: Santa Caterina Martire (Russian Orthodox)
sights.blurb: Gold onion domes in the Russian embassy's park, looking across at St Peter's: the first purpose-built Russian Orthodox church in Rome.
sights.q: Chiesa di Santa Caterina Martire, Via del Lago Terrione 77

sights.name: Latter-day Saints Temple, Settebagni
sights.blurb: A North American-style temple of 2019 with two spires on a 6-hectare estate; the visitor centre is laid out like a Roman forum.
sights.when: Grounds and visitor centre Tue–Sat (Google, 2026); free. Non-members cannot enter the temple itself.
sights.q: Rome Italy Temple, Via di Settebagni 376

sights.name: San Valentino al Villaggio Olimpico
sights.blurb: A 1980s church of stacked cubes in the 1960 Olympic Village, a short walk from Nervi's viaduct.
sights.q: Chiesa di San Valentino, Viale XVII Olimpiade

sights.name: Sant'Ugo
sights.blurb: A 1989–91 parish church in Val Melaina that Italian Wikipedia counts among Rome's brutalist churches.
sights.when: Parish hours.
sights.q: Chiesa di Sant'Ugo, Viale Lina Cavalieri 3

sights.name: Santissimo Nome di Maria in Via Latina
sights.blurb: A reinforced-concrete parish church near the Caffarella, listed among Rome's brutalist churches.
sights.when: Parish hours.
sights.q: Santissimo Nome di Maria in Via Latina, Via Centuripe 16

sights.name: SS. Corpo e Sangue di Cristo
sights.blurb: Aldo Aloysi and Ernesto Vichi's 1989–91 church of exposed concrete in the Prenestino.
sights.when: Parish hours.
sights.q: Chiesa Santissimo Corpo e Sangue di Cristo, Via Narni 19

sights.name: Sacro Cuore del Suffragio and the Purgatory museum
sights.blurb: A neo-Gothic "little Milan Cathedral" by the Tiber, with one glass case of scorch marks said to be left by souls in Purgatory.
sights.when: Free; roughly 7:30–11:00 and 16:30–19:30 (sources conflict).
sights.q: Museo delle Anime del Purgatorio, Lungotevere Prati 12

sights.name: Corviale ("Il Serpentone")
sights.blurb: A single concrete housing block a kilometre long on the edge of the countryside: Rome's answer to the Falowiec.
sights.when: A lived-in building; outside and the public spaces freely walkable. Be discreet with cameras.
sights.q: Corviale, Via di Poggio Verde, Roma

sights.name: Laurentino 38 and its "bridges"
sights.blurb: A 1970s–80s estate on a 4 km ring road, crossed by "bridge-buildings" that were meant to hold shops and became Rome's most stigmatised addresses.
sights.when: Public streets. The first bridge is the Municipio IX office; bridges 5 and 6 are building sites.
sights.q: Viale Ignazio Silone, Laurentino 38

sights.name: Tuscolano: Libera's "horizontal unit" and the INA-Casa estate
sights.blurb: Adalberto Libera's walled "kasbah" of patio houses (1950–54), inside Rome's biggest INA-Casa estate, where Pasolini shot Mamma Roma.
sights.when: A lived-in courtyard entered through a vaulted gate on Via Selinunte; be discreet. The estate streets are public.
sights.q: Via Selinunte, Tuscolano, Roma

sights.name: Borgata Quarticciolo
sights.blurb: The last Fascist borgata (1940–43), laid out like a Roman army camp; its tower was the Fascist party house, then a police station.
sights.when: Public streets; included in Open House Roma.
sights.q: Piazza del Quarticciolo, Roma

sights.name: Villaggio Olimpico and the Corso Francia viaduct
sights.blurb: The 1960 athletes' village on pilotis, with Nervi's viaduct on "butterfly" piers carrying the road over it.
sights.when: Public streets; walk under the viaduct. Map pin approximate.
sights.q: Viadotto di Corso Francia, Villaggio Olimpico, Roma

sights.name: Tor di Valle racecourse
sights.blurb: Julio Lafuente's 1959 grandstand of concrete "umbrellas", crumbling behind a broken wall since the racecourse closed in 2013.
sights.when: Not legally enterable: fenced, partly squatted, asbestos. View through gaps from Via del Mare / Via dell'Ippica.
sights.q: Ippodromo Tor di Valle, Roma

sights.name: Vela di Calatrava, Tor Vergata
sights.blurb: The 75 m white ribbed "sail" of Calatrava's unfinished swimming stadium, abandoned for 15 years and handed back to the city in 2025.
sights.when: The park is open; the structures by event only.
sights.q: Vela di Calatrava, Tor Vergata

sights.name: Stadio Flaminio
sights.blurb: Pier Luigi and Antonio Nervi's 1959 stadium, closed since 2011, with a cantilevered ribbed canopy behind fences and weeds.
sights.when: Closed; view from the street.
sights.q: Stadio Flaminio, Roma

sights.name: Palazzetto dello Sport
sights.blurb: Nervi and Vitellozzi's 1957 ribbed dome on Y-shaped buttresses, put up in 40 days from 1,620 precast pieces.
sights.when: Exterior always; interior at events.
sights.q: Palazzetto dello Sport, Piazza Apollodoro 10

sights.name: EUR: Palazzo della Civiltà Italiana
sights.blurb: The "Square Colosseum" and the stripped-classical streets of the world's fair Mussolini never held.
sights.when: Streets always; the Palazzo's interior only during exhibitions (Fendi headquarters).
sights.q: Palazzo della Civiltà Italiana, Quadrato della Concordia

sights.name: Foro Italico and Stadio dei Marmi
sights.blurb: Mussolini's sports forum: a marble stadium ringed by 60 colossal athletes and an obelisk still reading MUSSOLINI DUX.
sights.when: Open grounds; the stadium is often free to walk or run in.
sights.q: Stadio dei Marmi, Viale dei Gladiatori

sights.name: Ex Velodromo Olimpico crater
sights.blurb: The 1960 Olympic velodrome was blown up in 2008 with 120 kg of explosive; a fenced green void of 6.6 hectares is all that is left.
sights.when: Fence and street only.
sights.q: Viale della Tecnica, EUR

sights.name: The Termini–Centocelle railway
sights.blurb: The narrow-gauge "trenino giallo" of 1916 ran down the Via Casilina for 110 years; it closed for good in March 2026, and its tracks are already a ruin.
sights.when: Street; pin at Porta Maggiore, where the line ran under the Roman gate. Approximate.
sights.q: Porta Maggiore, Roma

sights.name: Ex Ospedale Forlanini
sights.blurb: A 1930s tuberculosis city of 280,000 m², closed in 2015, still paying huge water bills, now rented as a film set.
sights.when: Closed; exterior from the street. Pin approximate (next to the working San Camillo hospital).
sights.q: Ospedale Forlanini, Circonvallazione Gianicolense, Roma

sights.name: Santa Maria della Pietà and the Museo della Mente
sights.blurb: Europe's largest asylum (1913): a park of numbered pavilions, some still derelict and painted by street artists, with a museum of the mind in Pavilion 6.
sights.when: Park open in daylight; museum Tue–Sat 9:00–16:00 (Google, 2026), booking advised.
sights.q: Museo Laboratorio della Mente, Piazza di Santa Maria della Pietà 5

sights.name: Ex Penicillina
sights.blurb: Italy's first penicillin plant, opened in 1950 with Alexander Fleming present; abandoned since 2006, sold in 2025, waiting for demolition.
sights.when: Closed and dangerous; exterior only from Via Tiburtina. Probably gone within a few years.
sights.q: Ex Penicillina, Via Tiburtina 1040

sights.name: Ex Mira Lanza
sights.blurb: An 1899 soap and chemical works by the Tiber: pyrite furnaces, burnt sheds and murals by Seth, about to become student housing.
sights.when: Exterior; Teatro India, in part of the old works, has events.
sights.q: Forni pirite ex Mira Lanza, Lungotevere Vittorio Gassman

sights.name: Gazometro and Ostiense
sights.blurb: The steel skeleton of Europe's largest gasholder of 1937, 90 m tall: the icon of industrial Rome.
